researchLibrary.title: NDSU Langdon white-mold trial
researchLibrary.design: Four randomized blocks; spring canola; 20% bloom application, irrigation and natural infection.
researchLibrary.finding: Under low disease pressure, disease, yield and test-weight differences were not statistically significant.
researchLibrary.limits: Drought limited disease; a null result in this setting does not establish equivalence across products.

researchLibrary.title: NDSU Langdon white-mold trial
researchLibrary.design: Four randomized blocks; spring canola; irrigation, inoculation and 20% bloom application.
researchLibrary.finding: Disease incidence and severity differed among treatments; yield and test weight did not differ significantly.
researchLibrary.limits: One site-year. The trial table includes a Propulse rate above the reviewed canola label and a dry-product unit issue; experimental rates are not use directions.

researchLibrary.title: NDSU Langdon white-mold trial
researchLibrary.design: Four randomized blocks; one spring-canola cultivar; irrigation and inoculation; 20% bloom, 20 GPA.
researchLibrary.finding: Disease measures differed, but yield differences were not statistically significant.
researchLibrary.limits: A single spring-canola site-year cannot establish general winter-canola rankings. Research-table rate/unit issues are not copied to profiles.

researchLibrary.title: NDSU Langdon white-mold trial
researchLibrary.design: Four randomized blocks; one spring-canola cultivar; irrigation and inoculation; 20% bloom, 20 GPA.
researchLibrary.finding: Untreated disease incidence was 73%; treated plots were 0–25%. Disease differences were significant; yield and test weight were not.
researchLibrary.limits: Single site-year. Experimental rates and a Topsin treatment are not winter-canola recommendations.

researchLibrary.title: Minnesota Canola Production Center disease-management trials
researchLibrary.design: Roseau and St. Paul; four randomized blocks, one hybrid, infested hulls; conventional and biological programs.
researchLibrary.finding: Responses varied by site. A sequential conventional program performed well at Roseau; St. Paul had low disease and severe lodging. Biological results were variable.
researchLibrary.limits: All Roseau plots received Priaxor after hail: the “untreated” row was untreated by the experimental bloom program, not wholly fungicide-free. Site conditions limit generalization.

researchLibrary.title: Multi-location canola fungicide study (Bradley and colleagues)
researchLibrary.finding: Disease suppression varied by location and season; disease reduction did not consistently translate to higher yield.
researchLibrary.limits: Historical products and research rates do not establish current permission. Full paper was not reviewed. DOI: 10.1094/PD-90-1129.

researchLibrary.title: Bloom timing and fungicide programs (Khangura & van Burgel)
researchLibrary.design: Thirteen Western Australian field trials over eight years.
researchLibrary.finding: Applications within 10–50% bloom generally outperformed very early or late timing; yield response depended on disease pressure. Single sprays were more economical than doubles under the study assumptions.
researchLibrary.limits: Foreign production systems, prices and labels. This is supporting timing evidence, not U.S. application authorization; full paper not reviewed. DOI: 10.1007/s42360-021-00321-7.

researchLibrary.title: Saskatchewan fungicide sensitivity and water-volume project
researchLibrary.design: Near Yorkton; fungicide and water-volume comparisons; sensitivity screening described as ongoing.
researchLibrary.finding: Higher water volume improved coverage, but low Sclerotinia and Verticillium confounding limited disease/yield interpretation. No significant treatment differences were reported in the summarized field results.
researchLibrary.limits: The planned isolate report due December 2026 was not available as of November 13. The summary does not demonstrate fungicide resistance or justify a rate change.

researchLibrary.title: Missouri winter-canola disease guidance
researchLibrary.design: Regional production guidance, reviewed March 2026; not a comparative fungicide trial.
researchLibrary.finding: White mold is a principal winter-canola disease locally. The publication says routine preventive fungicide applications usually do not pay under Missouri conditions.
researchLibrary.limits: Regional economic guidance must be interpreted with field risk and current costs; it is not a national no-spray rule.

researchLibrary.title: South Dakota 2026 oilseed pest-management guide
researchLibrary.finding: Useful for finding additional canola products and supporting sources.
researchLibrary.limits: Some dry-product rates are printed with fluid units. Use exact product labels for application quantities; the regional roster is not automatically a winter-canola approval.

coverageGaps.detail: EPA master uses can differ from final brand/container labels; distributor names are indexed, but every container label and current stock are not audited.
56 state/territorial directory entries and a verification workflow are provided. Product approval, Section 24(c), Section 18, tribal requirements and expirations need location-specific review.
Every tracked record has a review status. Text screening is not full label interpretation; image-only tables and crop groups can require more review.
U.S., Canadian and Australian evidence is distinguished. Site-years, abstracts and project summaries are not pooled into a universal efficacy score. All possible publications have not been retrieved.

196 tracked EPA records, 122 primary profile PDFs and two Extension feeds are checked. The check does not crawl every new registration, state database or research publication. Failures remain visible.
Blackleg, Alternaria and other diseases, seed/soil uses, bee-vectored delivery and non-U.S. product permissions are not merged into the winter-canola foliar white-mold table.
